input.content: Pattern: independently released client starts REQUIRING a new provider response field (e.g. a receipt like `applied: True`) before the supported released provider emits it. Every ordinary call then fails even though the provider applied the change. A feature flag (e.g. enhanced_settings) gives no protection when the new check is not gated on it. The regression hides because the unit-test fake provider is rewritten to return the future contract, so no test still exercises the released provider's actual response shape. Review check: compare each newly required response key with the released provider source at the supported tag, and keep a test that mirrors the legacy response. Fix shape: treat an absent field as the legacy acknowledgement (only when the legacy success already implies the guarantee) and reject only an explicit negative, or negotiate capability. (Seen: enhanced-settings Task 1, client.py receipt check vs eval-release provider/settings.py.)
